_comment: Permissions granted to the ECS AGENT, not to the application
(executionRoleArn in deploy/ecs-task-definition.json).
The agent uses these before and around the container: pull the image,
resolve the `secrets` block, open a log stream. The application never gets
them -- that is the entire point of ECS having two roles, and why the
task role in this directory contains no ECR and no Secrets Manager access.
A compromised container therefore cannot read the HMAC secret from
Secrets Manager; it only ever sees the one value already in its own
environment.
Shared by all four PNSM services (AI, API, and the two frontends), which is
why the ECR statement is repository-scoped by name prefix rather than to a
single repository.
Placeholders in ANGLE BRACKETS are filled by scripts/provision_aws.py.
GetAuthorizationToken cannot be resource-scoped -- it is an account
level call that returns a 12-hour registry token. This is an AWS API
shape, not a shortcut: the pull itself is scoped by the next statement.
CreateLogGroup is here because the task definition sets
awslogs-create-group=true, so the group is made on first launch rather
than being a manual prerequisite that gets forgotten during a rebuild.
Enumerated one ARN per secret, not `pnsm/*`. A wildcard would silently
widen the grant the moment somebody stores a fifth secret under the
same prefix -- for instance the MongoDB Atlas connection string, which
the AI service has no business reading.
Secrets Manager encrypts with KMS, so reading a secret needs a Decrypt
the agent would otherwise be denied. Bound to via-service so this role
cannot use the key for anything except unsealing a secret.
